etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English symphonye, from Old French simphonie, from Latin symphonia, from Ancient Greek συμφωνία (sumphōnía). By surface analysis, sym- +‎ -phony. Doublet of sinfonia, symphonia, tsampouna, and zampogna.

definitions.definition: An extended piece of music of sophisticated structure, usually for orchestra.
(music) An instrumental introduction or termination to a vocal composition.
Harmony in music or colour, or a harmonious combination of elements.
